rows.label: PROPOSAL · question 28 (my pick)
rows.text: Whenever you create or apply a federation rule, it's best practice to store the full case history so it can be re-evaluated in future: what happened, the principles that actually conflicted, your first judgments, and your final decision and rationale. Any dissenting opinions should go in there as well, along with the consequences in the case. When the rule changes because of a new case, run the old case through again to see how it would turn out. That saves each generation from having to rediscover the same constitutional fight from scratch.
